C1_successor_obligations.claim: Matching-lift algebra and normalization remain sound.
C1_successor_obligations.assessment: Mean-one symmetric regular K gives a symmetric mean-one matching average with exact one-coordinate regularity and pair coefficient lambda=1/(r-1) for even r, 1/r for odd r. The private-port density identity and positive edge-subset weights remain unchanged. Proper-subset error costs at most epsilon*(1-lambda^66), and the full gain is c0*lambda^66. Choosing epsilon<=c0*lambda^66/2 retains an r^-66 relative deficit. A polynomial K supremum raised to floor(r/2) only gives mean at least r^-Cr under the current bound, not r^-C.

C1_successor_obligations.claim: The weaker mean gives the stated excess scale.
C1_successor_obligations.assessment: Delta>=c*r^-66 and -log p<=C*r*log r give kernel excess at least c'/(r^67*log r). The eventual 0<p<1 and positive density conditions follow from bounded normalization and the strict-deficit pair profile for large r. Finite-host approximation remains acknowledged separate.

C2_successor_obligations.assessment: For the same fixed atom and every sufficiently large integer r, the question requests both polynomial alphabet |Omega|<=r^C and polynomial mean p>=r^-C while retaining relative deficit at least c*r^-66. Constants c,C are independent of r. The fixed atom, symmetry, regularity, [0,1] range and noninjective hom-density convention remain explicit.

The matching route supplies the r^-66 deficit but only an r^-Cr mean bound. The single-pair route supplies polynomial mean but only an r^-132 deficit. Combining their separate conclusions does not supply one kernel with both stronger properties. Failure or a loose/exponential normalization bound for one chosen construction is not proof that all alternative witnesses fail.

C2_successor_obligations.claim: Improved excess if the stronger target holds
C2_successor_obligations.assessment: The same logarithmic argument now uses -log p<=C*log r, giving c'/(r^66*log r). This is a conditional consequence, not evidence that the desired target exists.

The stated condition is logically sufficient: for every fixed C, along some unbounded integer sequence r, the supremum positive relative deficit over all eligible uniform symmetric regular kernels with the two C-bounds is o(r^-66). If C2 held with constants c,C,r0, its witnesses would force this supremum to be at least c*r^-66 at every sufficiently large r, contradicting the chosen sequence for that C. The kernel class is nonempty (the constant-one kernel on a one-point space), and p>=r^-C excludes division by zero. This is sufficient, not asserted necessary or established.

C2 is expressly unproved, with no certified novelty, established-openness or sharpness claim. Two materially distinct routes remain visible: better normalization/control of a regular lift, or a different bounded regular witness. No desired existence is silently assumed.
